rows.32:2fcc:
Tachibana hesitated.
She couldn't just stand by and watch Tsukahara in trouble.
But if she showed herself, he might not like it.
In the end, though, she couldn't bear to watch him struggle any longer, and she rushed out.{p}
rows.32:30a4:
"...Um, please use this umbrella."
At first he looked annoyed to see her, but he soon smiled.
"Oh, thanks. Wanna walk home together?"
She hadn't meant to walk home with him.
Even so, he insisted on sharing the umbrella with her.{p}
rows.32:31a0:
She felt terribly awkward.
Even so, he went on chattering as he pleased.
"Hey, sorry about all that.
I just haven't had any time lately.
I'm busy, y'know, with this and that. You get it, right?
I just wanna be nice to everybody.
It's not like I'm in love with anyone or anything.
See? So it's not like I started hating you, Yukari..."{p}
rows.32:32ec:
As he said that, he suddenly tried to kiss her.
"Please stop."
Startled by the sudden move, Tachibana refused him.
She still loved him even now, but she already knew he had only been toying with her.
She believed that kissing was wrong unless two people loved each other.
So she shoved Tsukahara away.{p}
rows.32:3440:
Frankly, he was taken aback.
No girl had ever turned him down before.
At first he tried to laugh it off, but his pride had been badly wounded.
So he attacked her.
"Don't you screw with me!"
Tachibana was shocked.
The Tsukahara she had thought so kind was coming at her with a monstrous face.{p}
rows.32:3588:
She swung the umbrella around wildly.
"Stop!
Please stop!"
Suddenly she felt a dull impact in her hands.
The hands holding the umbrella abruptly grew heavy, as if it had caught on something.
"Gyaah..."
...Tsukahara was groaning.{p}
rows.32:3678:
When she looked, the tip of the umbrella was stuck in his left eye.
The blood pouring out of it was carving a red pattern into the blue umbrella.
"...Y-you bitch.
I'll fucking kill you!"{p}
rows.32:37ec:
Terrified beyond words, Tachibana squeezed her eyes shut and just kept thrusting the umbrella out.
Not knowing what she was doing, she thrust it out again and again.{p}
rows.32:386c:
Each time, she felt it strike something heavy.
The feel of it plunging into something heavy and soft...{p}
rows.32:38f0:
After a while, Tachibana fearfully opened her eyes.
Tsukahara lay sprawled in front of her.
He didn't move a muscle; his face and body had been stabbed all over, and he lay dead, drenched in blood.
His face was a pulpy mess, as if birds had pecked at it, with flaps of flesh peeled back here and there.
When she looked, the blue umbrella was dyed bright red too.
But strangely, she wasn't afraid.
She had fallen flat on her bottom; leaning on the red-stained blue umbrella, she staggered to her feet.
Then she stabbed the umbrella into Tsukahara's utterly still corpse, again and again.
Humming a tune as she did.
And then she killed herself.{p}
rows.32:3b24:
They say she was found dead with the umbrella stabbed into her own throat.
They say a person normally can't drive an umbrella into their own throat.
It would hurt too much to go through with it, wouldn't it?
But she saw it through.
When she was found, they say her throat had been pierced clean through, from front to back.
She must have thought she had to die.
And she must have thought that the more pain she felt, the more her sin would be atoned for.
That's why she endured the pain and drove the umbrella in, I suppose.
That's what I think.{p}
rows.32:3cf4:
It was all written off as a woman in a messy breakup who killed the man and then killed herself after him.
Even though that's not what really happened.{p}
rows.32:3d70:
...The strange thing, though, was the murder weapon left at the scene: the blue umbrella.
At first, they say, everyone thought it was a red umbrella.
Why? Because even though it had been raining, the blood on the umbrella hadn't washed off.
They say the color had set in, as if the umbrella had been dyed through.{p}
rows.32:3e80:
...And that's the end of Tachibana's story.
...But they say that after Tachibana died, something strange began to appear.{p}
rows.32:3f00:
On rainy days, they say, a high-school girl with an umbrella stands quietly by the school gate.
As if she's lying in wait for someone who has no umbrella.
And they say that sometimes she's holding a blue umbrella and a red umbrella.
I wonder who on earth she could be.
...Though I have a fair idea.{p}
rows.32:4028:
{a}, you might want to be careful.
I'm sure Tachibana has had enough of men like Tsukahara by now.
Next time, she might fall for a boy like you.
...But you said you thought Tachibana was a strange girl, didn't you?
You'd better be careful.
The more devoted and earnest a girl is, the less you can tell what she'll do when you make her angry.
Whatever you do, be careful when a girl confesses her feelings to you.
If you think you can just play around with her for fun... If it were me, I'd kill you.
Heh heh...
Now, shall we hear the next person's story?{p}
rows.32:4210:
My, you're quite sure of yourself.
Anyone with ordinary sensibilities wouldn't go around calling themselves cool.
And yet you... That's a little surprising.
But you know, that kind of attitude isn't good.
I don't like it.
...Well, never mind.
Let me ask you one more thing.{p}
rows.32:430c:
My, that's not true.
I think you're not bad at all.
Still, you're far more likable than someone who calls himself cool.
I like people like that, heh heh...
May I ask you one more strange question?{p}
rows.32:43dc:
I see, so you like the rain.
Come to think of it, I know a story about someone who loved the rain, just like you.
His name was Hata, I believe.
Hata was a student at this school.
He was earnest and kind, and his grades were decent, upper-middle or so.
But he wasn't popular with girls.
As for why... it's a little hard to say.{p}
rows.32:4518:
He was by no means handsome.
Girls just can't help judging by appearances, can they?
To me, that seems nothing but foolish.
But the girls, unable to see the beauty inside him, paid Hata no attention at all.{p}By the way, {a}, are you interested in girls?
rows.32:46bc:
Hata was the same.
But he had his friends.
So even if the girls wouldn't give him the time of day, he didn't get too anxious about it.
There were other things he loved, too.
And among the many things he loved, just like you, {a}, was the rain.{p}
rows.32:47c4:
He loved the rain.
So much that he didn't mind going without an umbrella, even in a downpour.
Then, one day...
That day, a fine drizzle had been falling since morning.
To him, that hardly even counted as rain.
He had an umbrella his family had forced on him, but he couldn't be bothered to open it, so he walked along getting wet.{p}
rows.32:48e0:
Then he saw a girl sheltering from the rain under the eaves of a shop.
She was looking up at the sky, lost and on the verge of tears.
Her helpless expression was so cute that Hata went over to her without thinking.
When she noticed him, the girl flinched and backed away.
Flustered, Hata pressed his umbrella into her hands.{p}
rows.32:49f0:
"Please use this."
The girl looked at him in surprise.
He could see himself reflected in her large, glossy eyes.
Hata turned red.
But it would be odd to take the umbrella back now, wouldn't it?{p}
rows.32:4aa8:
Practically flinging the umbrella at her, Hata broke into a run.
The girl watched his back for a long, long time.{p}
rows.32:4b2c:
The next day, it was raining too.
On his way home from school without an umbrella, Hata met her again.{p}
rows.32:4c20:
Smiling sweetly, she held out the umbrella she had borrowed from Hata.
"Y-you don't need it anymore?"
Hata's voice came out high and shaky.
She smiled and nodded.
That smile was warm and gentle, overflowing with affection.
She likes me.
...That's what Hata thought.{p}
rows.32:4d4c:
When he headed home with his umbrella back, he realized she hadn't said a single word.
But he thought nothing more of it than that she must be shy.
After that, the girl began waiting for Hata on his way home.
Strangely, though, only on rainy days.{p}
rows.32:4e48:
What's more, she was always in front of the same shop.
They would stand there and talk... though he was the only one who talked.
When he'd said all he had to say, she would see him off and he'd head home. That happened several times.
Even so, Hata was happy.
Just seeing her smile made him happy from the bottom of his heart.
But people are greedy creatures, aren't they?
Just once, Hata wanted to try this thing called a date.
So one day, he asked her out.{p}
rows.32:4ff0:
"Will you go on a date with me?"
...Like that.
She fell silent and looked down.
When he asked what was wrong, she didn't answer.
She just bit her lip, looking troubled.
Hata had been sure she would say yes, so it came as a shock.
She had always listened happily to whatever he said.
So Hata had believed she liked him.
But come to think of it, he had never actually heard it from her own lips.
Burning with shame and shock, Hata lost his temper.
"W-were you just making fun of me?"{p}
rows.32:52e4:
Her wet body was melting into sludge.
There was no trace left of her lovely face.
She melted away without the slightest resistance, like ice doused with hot water.
Right before Hata's eyes, she vanished without a trace.
He didn't understand what had happened.
But she hadn't been human.
Hata screamed and ran home.{p}
rows.32:54e0:
But... she was there.
Wearing her usual meek smile.{p}
rows.32:55b0:
Then he caught his breath and looked up.
There was a small shop in front of him.
And under its eaves was... her.
Had she gotten there ahead of him?
Hata lost his head.
And to get away from her, he dashed out into the street.{p}
rows.32:56b8:
...After he was hit by the car, they say Hata was struggling desperately.
As if he were desperately trying to escape from something.
The witnesses said he had suddenly dashed out into the street.
...That's right.
Strangely, it seems no one but Hata could see her.
What was she, really?
Why was Hata the one she clung to?
I don't know...
Maybe strange things come out on rainy days.{p}
rows.32:585c:
You'd better be careful too, {a}.
If you go wandering around just because you like the rain, something strange might take a liking to you.
Heh heh...
That's the end of my story.
Now, who's next?{p}
rows.32:590c:
My, you're not?
{a}, you're a late bloomer, aren't you?
Or... you're not going to tell me you prefer boys, are you?
...Well, never mind.
Anyway, most high-school boys are interested in girls.{p}
rows.32:5a2c:
I'll ask you one more time, so pick one or the other.
Now, do you like the rain?{p}Or do you hate it?
rows.32:5a9c:
My, you don't use one?
That's right, that's the correct answer.
Going out of your way to keep the precious rain off with an umbrella is just stupid.
You understand that, don't you?
I'm so glad.
To meet a kindred spirit in a place like this.{p}
rows.32:5b60:
Honestly, saying you hate the rain... that was cruel of you.
...No, I'm not angry.
Quite the opposite, I'm glad.
You like getting wet in the rain too, don't you?
Yes, I understand.
I knew it from the moment I first saw you.
That's right, you like the rain.
Of course you do.{p}
rows.32:5c74:
I'm sure we'll get along well.
After all, we both love the rain.
In that case, shall I tell you a story about the rain?
You'll be pleased, won't you, {a}?
Have you ever seen people standing by the shoe lockers on a rainy day, saying they're waiting out the rain?
There are plenty of people like that, aren't there?{p}
rows.32:5d68:
Hmm, so you play it by ear?
You say that, but maybe you're really just a sloppy sort who uses an umbrella when you have one and walks home wet when you forget it.
Oh, did that annoy you?
I'm joking, just joking... heh heh.
Well then, may I ask you something?{p}{a}, do you keep a spare umbrella at school?

notes: 32:4028: 'you said you thought Tachibana was a strange girl' is shown after all four answers to 32:2d74-2da4 (the source's 2db8 also assumes 'strange'); kept as written.
32:5b60: no follows_choice; it reads as the 'dislike rain' (32:0a3c) route continuing after 'no umbrella' (32:0ce8)/5a9c; rendered as a mild reproach.
